newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve flattens over past week - Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve flattens over past week - Delphis.

text.p: The municipal yield curve flattened over the week ended Thursday, as average yields on one-year munis held steady and 30-year yields fell five basis points, Delphis Hanover Corp said Friday.

The Aaa curve flattened five basis points for the second consecutive week, with the spread between one-year and 30-years dropping to 185 basis points. The spread between one-year and 30-year Baa's also fell five basis points to 185 basis points.

Thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields were five basis points lower for the fourth consecutive week, moving to 5.45 percent. Thirty-year Baa yields were also five basis points lower, at 6.25 percent, and have shed a total of 25 basis points over the past month.

The curve flattened because one-year munis missed out on the improvement. Average yields on one-year Aaa-rated and Baa-rated municipal bonds were unchanged for the second consecutive week, holding at 3.60 percent and 4.40 percent, respectively.

The muni market outperformed Treasuries over the week, as the government long bond yield was unchanged at 6.42 percent. It stood at 6.85 percent one month ago. Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis were yielding 84.9 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday.

In the intermediate sector of the municipal curve, ten-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds shed five basis points for the second week in a row, moving to 4.70 percent, and Baa-rated muni yields lost five to 5.55 percent.

The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged for the eighth consecutive week at 80 basis points. The 30-year spread was also unchanged at 80, after widening five the week before.
